facts.statement: About 5% of people with lymphoma develop a form of the disease that affects the central nervous system.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: When this type of lymphoma affects the spinal cord, it is uncommon, which makes it hard to diagnose early.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study describes a single patient whose first signs of the disease were in the spinal cord.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Magnetic resonance imaging showed multiple areas of abnormality in the neck and lower back parts of the patient's spinal cord.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: A whole-body PET/CT scan showed high activity in the spinal cord, liver, and kidneys.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Doctors confirmed the diagnosis by examining tissue samples taken from the patient's kidney and liver under a microscope.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors compared the imaging results and fluid markers of this secondary lymphoma with those of a primary form of the disease.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The goal of the comparison was to help doctors recognize this rare condition sooner.
facts.subject: humans
